newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dec JGB ends Tokyo up, cash yield curve steepens.
newsitem.headline: Dec JGB ends Tokyo up, cash yield curve steepens.

text.p: The key December Japanese Government Bond (JGB) contract ended Tokyo firmer, but the cash market was easier in late Wednesday trade, with the long-end of the curve suffering most losses, traders said.
"Despite small lot purchases and recoveries in futures, the cash market, particularly the long-end, fell down on its knees and refused to stand up straight," said a trader at a city bank.
The yield of the most recently issued 189th bond was 2.805 percent, up from 2.790 percent on Tuesday. The benchmark 183nd yield was 2.740 percent, down from 2.745 percent on Tuesday.
There were talk that an agricultural bank took profit in the long-end of the JGBs in early trading.
The key December ended at a day high of 123.27, up from Tuesday's 123.15. Turnover was 31,037 contracts.
Traders said the market remained interested in possible JGB purchases by funds set up to wind up failed mortgage firms.

They said cash totalling approximately 907 billion yen would be disbursed by banks on October 17 to the Financial Stabilisation Fund set up at the government's Deposit Insurance Corp in July. Some said the Fund might have bought 20-year JGBs offered on Tuesday.
The 20-year JGB auction was successful with lowest bids accepted at 100.50 and the average at 100.55. Half the offered amount has already been absorbed by investors, traders said.

The largest chunk of the money that will become available under the government mortgage firm scheme is the 2.7 trillion yen Japan's agricultural financial institutions are expected to receive, possibly in late November, traders said.
Some market participants expect at least half of this money to flow into bonds.

However, it remains to be seen whether such a hefty commitment to bonds will materialise. Others said these cash flows into JGBs had already been priced into the market leading to a fall in the benchmark JGB yield to 2.71 percent.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) continued to absorb JGBs from the market via its bond buying operations. The BOJ has bought 600 billion yen in long-term bonds since October 1.

"The central bank on the one hand appears concerned about the recent bond rally and the steep falls in long-term yields, but on the other, it keeps on buying bonds, making the supply of bonds quite tight," said a brokerage manager.
Many said that the BOJ's bond buying was in fact accentuating recent market euphoria.
The market remained nervous about remarks on interest rates by politicians ahead of Japan's general elections on October 20.

On Monday, Shizuka Kamei, publicity chief of the Liberal Democratic Party, was quoted by a U.S. news agency as saying that a rise in Japan's official discount rate may be considered after general elections.
